questions.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,y=u,\,z=u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

at the point where $u=1$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,1,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,0,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2},\,1,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2},\,0,\,1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=1$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{2})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=2u+v,\,y={u}^{2},\,z={v}^{2}
$$

at the point where $u=1$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u+v,\,{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2}⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2u,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{1}{2}) & =⟨2,\,2(1),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{1}{2}) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2(\frac{1}{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=1$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{1}{2})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-2,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x={v}^{2},\,y=2v,\,z=4u
$$

at the point where $u=\frac{1}{2}$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{v}^{2},\,2v,\,4u⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4u)⟩ \\  & =⟨2v,\,2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=\frac{1}{2}$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}) & =⟨0,\,0,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}) & =⟨2(\frac{1}{2}),\,2,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=\frac{1}{2}$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-8,\,4,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=1+{e}^{u},\,y=2-{e}^{v},\,z=1-{e}^{u}-{e}^{v}
$$

at the point where $u=1$ and $v=-1.$
questions.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨1+{e}^{u},\,2-{e}^{v},\,1-{e}^{u}-{e}^{v}⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(1+{e}^{u}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2-{e}^{v}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(1-{e}^{u}-{e}^{v})⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{u},\,0,\,-{e}^{u}⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(1+{e}^{u}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2-{e}^{v}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(1-{e}^{u}-{e}^{v})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-{e}^{v},\,-{e}^{v}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,-1) & =⟨{e}^{1},\,0,\,-{e}^{1}⟩ \\  & =⟨e,\,0,\,-e⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,-1) & =⟨0,\,-{e}^{-1},\,-{e}^{-1}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=1$ and $v=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,-1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,-1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ e & 0 & -e \\ 0 & -{e}^{-1} & -{e}^{-1}\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -e \\ -{e}^{-1} & -{e}^{-1}\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}e & -e \\ 0 & -{e}^{-1}\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}e & 0 \\ 0 & -{e}^{-1}\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,1,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:

$$
x=u+v,\,y={u}^{2}v,\,z=v

at the point where $u=1$ and $v=2.$

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,{u}^{2}v,\,v⟩.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2uv,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,{u}^{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨1,\,2(1)(2),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,4,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨1,\,(1)^{2},\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,2)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,-1,\,-3⟩.\end{aligned}

questions.problem: Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨1+v,\,uv,\,{u}^{2}⟩$ at the point $(2,1,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $(2,1,1)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}1+v=2 \\ uv=1 \\ {u}^{2}=1\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(1+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,v,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(1+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,u,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨0,\,1,\,2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point $(2,1,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨(1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u,\,(1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi ,
$$

 at the point $(1,1,\sqrt{3}).$

First, notice that since $(2,3,4)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}(1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡v=1 \\ u=1 \\ (1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡v=\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=\frac{\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}((1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}((1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,1,\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}((1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}((1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨(1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,0,\,-(1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{6}) & =⟨2(1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}),\,1,\,2(1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,\sqrt{3}⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{6}) & =⟨(1+(1)^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}),\,0,\,-(1+(1)^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{3},\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point $(1,1,\sqrt{3})$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{6})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & \sqrt{3} \\ \sqrt{3} & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & \sqrt{3} \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & \sqrt{3} \\ \sqrt{3} & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ \sqrt{3} & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,4,\,-\sqrt{3}⟩.\end{aligned}

questions.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,u+v,\,uv⟩$ at the point where $u=1$ and $v=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,1,\,v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2v,\,1,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=1$ and $v=1$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨2(1),\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,1,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨-2(1),\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-4,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=1$ and $v=1$ correspond to the point 

$$
({1}^{2}-{1}^{2},\,1+1,\,1\cdot 1)=(0,2,1),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,\,-4,\,4⟩\cdot ⟨x,\,y-2,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ 0\cdot x+(-4)\cdot (y-2)+4\cdot (z-1) & =0 \\ -4y+4z+4 & =0 \\ -y+z+1 & =0 \\ y-z & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨2{u}^{3},\,u{v}^{2},\,2v⟩$ at the point where $u=1$ and $v=3.$
questions.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2{u}^{3}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨6{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2{u}^{3}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2uv,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=1$ and $v=3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,3) & =⟨6(1)^{2},\,{3}^{2},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,9,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,3) & =⟨0,\,2(1)(3),\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,6,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,3)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,3) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 6 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 6 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}6 & 9 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨18,\,-12,\,36⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=1$ and $v=3$ correspond to the point 

$$
(2(1)^{3},\,1(3)^{2},\,2(3))=(2,9,6),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨18,\,-12,\,36⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-9,\,z-6⟩ & =0 \\ 18\cdot (x-2)-12\cdot (y-9)+36\cdot (z-6) & =0 \\ 18x-12y+36z-144 & =0 \\ 3x-2y+6z-24 & =0 \\ 3x-2y+6z & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u⟩$ at the point where $u=2$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨-u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=2$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(2,\frac{\pi }{2})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(2,\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=2$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}$ correspond to the point 

$$
(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2)=(0,2,2),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,\,-2,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨x,\,y-2,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ 0\cdot x+(-2)\cdot (y-2)+2\cdot (z-2) & =0 \\ -2y+2z & =0 \\ y-z & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,{u}^{3}-uv⟩$ at the point where $u=2$ and $v=6.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{3}-uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,3{u}^{2}-v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{3}-uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=2$ and $v=6:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,6) & =⟨1,\,0,\,3(2)^{2}-6⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,6⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,6) & =⟨0,\,1,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(2,6)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(2,6) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-6,\,2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=2$ and $v=6$ correspond to the point 

$$
(2,\,6,\,{2}^{3}-(2)(6))=(2,6,-4),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-6,\,2,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-6,\,z+4⟩ & =0 \\ (-6)\cdot (x-2)+2\cdot (y-6)+1\cdot (z+4) & =0 \\ -6x+2y+z+4 & =0 \\ 6x-2y-z & =4.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\pi ) & =⟨2,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ),\,8(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,8⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\pi ) & =⟨0,\,(1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}

$$
(2(1),\,(1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ),\,4(1)^{2})=(2,0,4),

questions.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x={u}^{2},\,y=2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,z=u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi ,
$$

at the point $(1,0,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi .
$$

First, notice that since $(1,0,1)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}=1 \\ 2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v=0 \\ u\operatorname{cos}⁡v=1\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=0.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-u\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,0) & =⟨2(1),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,0) & =⟨0,\,2(1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(0),\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,0)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,0) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,0,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-2,\,0,\,4⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ (-2)\cdot (x-1)+0\cdot y+4\cdot (z-1) & =0 \\ -2x+4z-2 & =0 \\ -x+2z-1 & =0 \\ x-2z & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,v⟩.
$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}u\operatorname{cos}⁡v=-2 \\ u\operatorname{sin}⁡v=0 \\ v=\pi \end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=2 \\ v=\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=2$ and $v=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,\pi ) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,\pi ) & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(2,\pi )\times {r}_{v}^{′}(2,\pi ) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨x+2,\,y,\,z-\pi ⟩ & =0 \\ 0\cdot (x+2)+1\cdot y+2\cdot (z-\pi ) & =0 \\ y+2z-2\pi  & =0 \\ y+2z & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=2$ and $v=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,1) & =⟨2(2),\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,1) & =⟨0,\,2(1),\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(2,1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(2,1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 4 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,-8,\,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-2,\,-8,\,8⟩\cdot ⟨x-4,\,y-1,\,z-4⟩ & =0 \\ (-2)\cdot (x-4)+(-8)\cdot (y-1)+8\cdot (z-4) & =0 \\ -2x-8y+8z-16 & =0 \\ -x-4y+4z-8 & =0 \\ x+4y-4z & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x=u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,y={u}^{2},\,z=2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi ,
$$

at the point $(0,1,-2).$
questions.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{u}^{2},\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi .
$$

First, notice that since $(0,1,-2)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}u\operatorname{sin}⁡v=0 \\ {u}^{2}=1 \\ 2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v=-2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,2u,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,0,\,-2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\pi ) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,2(1),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,-2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\pi ) & =⟨1\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,0,\,-2(1)\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,\pi )\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\pi ) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 2 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,\,2,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨x,\,y-1,\,z+2⟩ & =0 \\ 0\cdot x+2\cdot (y-1)+2\cdot (z+2) & =0 \\ 2y+2z+2 & =0 \\ y+z & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \big\langle v^2, \: u-v, \: u^2 \big\rangle$ at the point where $u=2$ and $v=-1.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2v,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=2$ and $v=-1{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,-1) & =⟨0,\,1,\,2(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,-1) & =⟨2(-1),\,-1,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(2,-1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(2,-1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ -2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,-8,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=2$ and $v=-1$ correspond to the point 

$$
\big( (-1)^2, \: 2-(-1), \: 2^2 \big) = (1, 3, 4),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,\,-8,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-3,\,z-4⟩ & =0 \\ 4\cdot (x-1)+(-8)\cdot (y-3)+2\cdot (z-4) & =0 \\ 4x-8y+2z+12 & =0 \\ 2x-4y+z+6 & =0 \\ 2x-4y+z & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$
